prompt: Write the body (about 120 words) of a letter of representation from a personal injury lawyer to an auto insurer. The client was hurt in a rear-end collision. Ask that all contact go through the law firm, ask for the policy limits, and ask the insurer to keep all evidence. No salutation, no signature, no names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1296; do not mention it.)
text:
This firm represents the individual injured in the rear-end collision described in your insured's claim file. Please direct all further communication regarding this matter to our office and do not contact our client directly, whether by telephone, mail, or in person. If your insured or any representative of your company has already been in contact with our client, please let us know so that we can address it.

We ask that you provide the bodily injury liability policy limits applicable to your insured for this loss, along with a copy of the declarations page confirming those limits. Please also identify any additional coverage that may apply, including excess or umbrella policies.

Our client's injuries are significant and ongoing, and treatment is continuing. We expect your company to take this claim seriously and to respond promptly.

Finally, we demand that your company preserve all evidence relating to this collision. This includes the claim file, photographs, recorded statements, telematics or dash camera footage, vehicle data, repair estimates, adjuster notes, and any communications with your insured or third parties. Failure to preserve this evidence may result in sanctions.
